s1.syndrome_frame: Fetal neurological abnormalities with ventriculomegaly and irregular ventricular walls
salient_findings: Multiple hyperechoic regions within the ventricular lumens
key_facts: Fetal Doppler ultrasound demonstrated normal middle cerebral artery perfusion
Fetal MRI confirmed bilateral ventricular enlargement
Areas of high signal intensity on T1-weighted images within the ventricles
Areas of low signal intensity on T2-weighted images within the ventricles
Comprehensive workup returned within normal limits

shortlist.label: Congenital Cytomegalovirus Infection
shortlist.why_kept: Fetal neurological abnormalities with ventriculomegaly and irregular ventricular walls are consistent with congenital CMV infection

shortlist.label: Dandy-Walker Malformation
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral ventriculomegaly and irregular ventricular walls are characteristic of Dandy-Walker malformation

shortlist.label: Lissencephaly
shortlist.why_kept: Fetal MRI findings of bilateral ventricular enlargement and areas of high signal intensity on T1-weighted images are consistent with lissencephaly

shortlist.label: Congenital Toxoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Fetal neurological abnormalities with ventriculomegaly and irregular ventricular walls are consistent with congenital toxoplasmosis

shortlist.label: Aicardi-Goutieres Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Fetal neurological abnormalities with ventriculomegaly and irregular ventricular walls, combined with normal comprehensive workup, are consistent with Aicardi-Goutieres syndrome

raw.rationale: The presence of bilateral ventriculomegaly, irregular ventricular walls, and multiple hyperechoic regions within the ventricles, along with areas of high signal intensity on T1-weighted images and low signal intensity on T2-weighted images within the ventricles on fetal MRI, are consistent with the findings of congenital CMV infection, which can cause ventriculomegaly and periventricular calcifications.

rejected.label: Dandy-Walker Malformation
rejected.why: Dandy-Walker malformation typically presents with hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis and cystic dilation of the fourth ventricle, which is not described in the case.

rejected.label: Lissencephaly
rejected.why: Lissencephaly is characterized by a smooth brain surface and thickened cortex, which is not consistent with the ultrasound and MRI findings in this case.

rejected.label: Congenital Toxoplasmosis
rejected.why: While congenital toxoplasmosis can cause ventriculomegaly and calcifications, the comprehensive workup, including a TORCH panel, returned within normal limits, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Aicardi-Goutieres Syndrome
rejected.why: Aicardi-Goutieres syndrome typically presents with calcifications in the basal ganglia and white matter, which is not described in the case, and often has a more severe clinical course.
